areas_reviewed: Decision (D), A4, A5, A6, and §0.6.6 claim state machine
C1 shared-document transaction and acceptance scenarios
append_audit, audit-chain verification/rebaseline, state loading, state.audit_sha, drift, and governance freshness
Versioning and ignore rules for WorkItem records
areas_not_reviewed: Unrelated refinement design such as lint rules, disputes, citations, iteration caps, and corpus measurement
Full test suite; no tests were run because this was a read-only consultation
An empirical Git merge reproduction; the audit-branch result was established from the hash-chain implementation

findings.claim: AGREE — drop decision (D)'s in-flight claim. Do not keep it in the versioned A6 index, and do not replace it with a local/gitignored claim. Across separate working copies it cannot provide live coordination and can travel later as stale state; within one working copy the short A5 mutex plus the edit's base-SHA precondition already prevents unsafe concurrent writes, while C1's shared-source acknowledgement supplies the human warning. Keep each origin's AWAITING_REASSESSMENT state and let changed content make every other sharer's assessment governance_stale.
findings.evidence: PLAN.md:231-245 makes the claim a long-lived A6-index field and relies on A5 only for check-and-claim serialization. CLAUDE.md:36 says WorkItem records are versioned except for two named local files, and .gitignore:9-11 does not ignore an A6 index; therefore an active claim can be committed and later imported into a checkout where its originating process and lock do not exist. Conversely, BRIEF.md:175-179 requires every edit to carry a base SHA and check it before writing. In one checkout, PLAN.md:299 already places apply's recheck under A5, so two stale applies cannot both commit. For post-edit safety, governance_freshness recomputes every recorded source SHA from disk on every call (scripts/sdle.py:5361-5405), and governance_precondition refuses a mismatch as governance_stale (scripts/sdle.py:9842-9864). A local claim would add orphan/cleanup state but no additional integrity guarantee: after A applies, B either has stale governance or can deliberately reassess the current document; before A applies, A5 plus the base SHA chooses one winner.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete decision (D) in §0.6.3 and all claim-only material in §0.6.6: the index loop field and claim states, refinement_document_in_flight, foreign-claim start checks, in-flight acknowledgement purposes, override/abandonment/STALE_BASE behavior, claim release/cancellation recovery, and their tests/docs. State explicitly that separate checkouts coordinate through Git publication plus digest revalidation, while A5 serializes same-checkout check-and-write operations. Retain the originating WorkItem's AWAITING_REASSESSMENT state, correlated reassessment, per-edit base SHA, C1 shared-source acknowledgement, and governance_stale for every other sharer.

findings.claim: AGREE — amend C1 so only the refining WorkItem's audit records the acknowledgement and names every other affected WorkItem. The two-writer problem is real across branches or clones. A deliberate engine-aware rechain can repair a merge, so Claude's statement that every hand-resolved merge necessarily remains broken is too absolute, but ordinary concatenation or conflict resolution is not chain-safe.
findings.evidence: append_audit reads the current ledger tail, hashes that tail into the new entry's Prev field, rewrites audit.md, and assigns the resulting whole-file hash to the supplied state object (scripts/sdle.py:1501-1526). Thus two branches appending after the same old tail create sibling entries with the same Prev; placing both sequentially makes the second link invalid, while choosing either branch leaves the other acknowledgement absent. Each branch also records a different audit_sha. audit verify independently requires both the whole-file SHA and every Prev link to match (scripts/sdle.py:1561-1618). read_state checks JSON and schema version but never audit_sha (scripts/sdle.py:1274-1316), and drift check reads state and artifact baselines without validating the audit ledger (scripts/sdle.py:10805-10835), so neither fails closed on this mismatch. Explicit audit rebaseline can rechain and save a new hash (scripts/sdle.py:1621-1661), but that is a repair operation, not a safe Git merge protocol. Cross-WorkItem appends also violate the stated single-writer invariant at CLAUDE.md:87.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend C1, BRIEF.md §3.5, scenarios 18 and 29, and §0.6 so the acknowledgement is stored in the refining WorkItem's transaction/refinement record and eventually its own audit, with the exact affected WorkItem ids. Remove all writes, deferred replay, locks, recovery steps, and idempotency checks targeting another WorkItem's audit/state. Use governance_stale as the safety notification. If proactive visibility is desired, derive a warning by reading the origin-owned transaction evidence when an affected WorkItem next runs; do not append to its chain or introduce another shared mutable notice ledger.

findings.claim: The current cross-audit design contradicts the brief's own scenario 12, which says WorkItem A's refinement cannot write WorkItem B's files, record, or decisions. Calling the audit append a special exception does not reconcile that unconditional acceptance criterion.
findings.evidence: BRIEF.md:374 forbids A from writing B's files. BRIEF.md:70, 186-200, and 382-403 simultaneously require A's shared edit to append and recover B's audit. PLAN.md:156 explicitly labels those audit writes a cross-WorkItem exception, confirming that the conflict is intentional rather than merely ambiguous.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve scenario 12 as the governing ownership rule and amend C1/scenarios 18 and 29 to require one origin-owned audit entry naming all affected WorkItems. Remove plan language creating a cross-WorkItem audit exception.

findings.claim: Claude is right that a divergent audit merge can fail audit verify, but wrong if implying state loading or drift will detect it automatically. Audit integrity is checked only by the explicit audit-verification path; ordinary state loading accepts an audit_sha mismatch.
findings.evidence: read_state returns after JSON and workflow-version checks without opening audit.md (scripts/sdle.py:1274-1316). verify_audit_chain is called only by cmd_audit_verify (scripts/sdle.py:1545-1592). cmd_drift_check calls read_state and compute_drift, then considers artifact baselines rather than audit_sha (scripts/sdle.py:10805-10835). Moreover, a later ordinary append replaces state.audit_sha with the current file hash (scripts/sdle.py:1523-1526); that can silently absorb a whole-file-only mismatch, although it cannot repair an already broken internal Prev link.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct §0.6's rationale to say cross-branch audit divergence is not rejected during normal state load or drift processing and is only diagnosed by audit verify. Use that as an additional reason to remove cross-WorkItem audit writes; do not claim existing loading or drift checks make them safe.

findings.claim: Claude overstates Git's protection by calling a simultaneous document edit an ordinary merge conflict. Disjoint edits can merge cleanly, and linked git worktrees share refs/object storage even though their working-tree files remain isolated. The reliable controls after integration are the document digest and base-SHA checks, not the existence of a merge conflict.
findings.evidence: BRIEF.md:175-180 permits anchored edits at arbitrary locations, so two branches need not touch the same merge hunk. The engine independently hashes current bound-source bytes (scripts/sdle.py:5371-5405) and refuses stale governance (scripts/sdle.py:9842-9864), while refinement edits carry an explicit base SHA (BRIEF.md:175-179). The inspected checkout is itself a linked worktree: its git directory is under the main repository's .git/worktrees directory while git-common-dir is the main .git directory; nevertheless its project root is a separate working directory.
findings.suggested_fix: State in §0.6 that Git is the publication/integration layer across checkouts but that a merge conflict is neither guaranteed nor required for safety. Pin safety to post-integration digest revalidation and per-edit base SHA checks.

findings.claim: If both recommendations are accepted, remove A6 and the multi-participant portions of the C1 transaction, but retain a simplified origin-local C1 transaction, A4 recovery, A5's short repository mutex, and AWAITING_REASSESSMENT.
findings.evidence: A6 exists to discover transaction participants and carry decision (D)'s claim (PLAN.md:156, 284-292); neither purpose remains when only the origin is written and D is deleted. However, even one origin still has a non-atomic document-write/audit-state sequence: append_audit explicitly documents append → hash → save-state ordering (scripts/sdle.py:1489-1492), and BRIEF.md:186-200 requires recovery around the document write. A4 therefore remains but becomes origin-local. A5 remains necessary in one shared working copy to serialize base-SHA check plus document write, requirements binding, init, and architecture's requirements recheck (PLAN.md:155, 299, 333-335). AWAITING_REASSESSMENT remains the origin's own loop guard and init precondition (PLAN.md:155, 166), independent of any foreign claim.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite A4 as an origin-owned transaction: durable intent and target evidence in refinement.json, base-SHA document write, origin audit/deferred replay, commit/abort, and recovery of the document/audit/state window. Delete A6 completely. Keep A5, but remove claim/index operations from its critical sections. Keep AWAITING_REASSESSMENT solely in the origin's refinement state and retain A16's refusal while that local loop is non-terminal. Update recovery tests from one-entry-per-WorkItem to exactly one origin audit entry naming all sharers.
